speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: The eighteenth, as you said when you came home. I have not grown it into a new promise.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The eighteenth. Letters, not a chest. The carrier has the day. I have not given him a second one.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: Then the pack can wait to be a pack. I am not sewing a speech into a shirt for the road.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Nothing extra. What you came with, and what the house is not sending as a chest.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Nothing extra. I will not invent an errand to have one.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: Is there a letter in it for me, or only the house's letters?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The house's letters, when there are any. I am not writing a child's letter to make a pack look full.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: Good. A full pack is how a shirt gets crushed, and I have mended enough heels this week.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: The bundle on the shelf has stayed tied since Monday's list. I am not asking you to open it this morning.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Nine days, and nothing of the play. The list was the house. I meant to write nothing, and I have written nothing.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: Monday's leaves are still under the weight. I can read them. They are salt and malt. They are not a girl at a window.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: They are salt and malt. Leave them salt and malt.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Then the morning is the eighteenth, and the letters, and a shelf that can stay a shelf.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: The eighteenth can arrive without being rehearsed at breakfast. I have said so, and I am saying so once more, and then I am done.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Once more is enough. Letters, not a chest. No second day. No errand invented before noon.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: And no reading of the tied bundle to show me you have not opened it. Tied is tied. I can see the knot.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: She can see the knot. So can I. Go and be in the house without making the road into this afternoon's work.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The road is the eighteenth. This afternoon is not the road, and it is not a new promise.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: Then eat, and let the knot alone. A knot that is talked of comes undone out of politeness.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: I will not talk of it. I have the queen in the shadow of the trees, and that book is enough for a Saturday.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Keep the book you have. I am not giving you the next thing, and I am not giving the carrier a chest.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Three weeks was the question, and the eighteenth was the answer, and both of them can sit down now.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Both of them are sitting. I have nothing to add to a date.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: Then add nothing. The porridge is the rest of the morning.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then I am adding nothing, and I am eating.
